debugger.dashboard.title: Hardware simulation and debugging
debugger.dashboard.subtitle: Independent workbench · STM32 / ST-Link / GDB
debugger.dashboard.attachNote: Attach to actual hardware. Firmware is never downloaded or flashed automatically.
debugger.dashboard.samplingNote: CPU data is sampled while the target is stopped. Running retains the last sample, rather than cycle-accurate simulation.
debugger.dashboard.architectureNote: This diagram illustrates the CPU execution structure. Addresses, registers and instructions come from actual debugger samples; unobserved pipelines and clock cycles are not displayed.
debugger.dashboard.noHardwareSample: Attach and stop the target to view actual CPU registers. No synthetic execution data is generated before sampling.
debugger.dashboard.changedNote: A blue background marks a register changed since the previous stopped sample.
debugger.dashboard.instructionEmpty: Stop the target to view actual disassembly around the PC. Step to observe changes in the PC and registers.
debugger.dashboard.stackEmpty: The call stack appears when the target is stopped. Function names and source lines depend on ELF symbols.
debugger.dashboard.breakpointsEmpty: When stopped, add breakpoints by function, source line or address.
debugger.dashboard.memoryNote: Read SRAM or Flash by address while the target is stopped. Values come from the connected chip, separately from the static firmware preview.
debugger.dashboard.memoryEmpty: Choose an address and byte count, then stop the target and read memory.
debugger.dashboard.storageNote: This view shows static load segments and bytes from the selected ELF, rather than live chip Flash. It does not imply the file has been flashed. Preview addresses are file offsets.
debugger.dashboard.storageEmpty: Select an ELF / AXF symbol file to inspect its static storage structure without connecting a device.
debugger.dashboard.logEmpty: GDB and server output appears here after starting a debug session.
settings.installOutputHint: Install tools or drivers to see the current stage, download progress, and output from third-party installers here.
